name: Declarative Web Push (Safari)
plain: A push format that shows a notification without running site code.
meaning: The browser renders the notification straight from JSON, so no service worker runs. Cuts battery use and removes the old silent-push abuse path; the site still learns when a device is online.

web.api: pushManager.subscribe via window; payload {"web_push": 8030, "notification": {title, navigate, body, lang, dir, silent, app_badge}}

access.prompt_ui: Same system notification prompt as classic Web Push; subscription made from the window with no service worker.
steps: Send JSON with web_push 8030 and a notification object

data.metric: Notification JSON handled by the browser

limits.headline: Can show you a notification from Safari's new push format without running site code
limits.user_action: You tap Allow on the notification pop up in Safari
can: Show a notification straight from the message, with no site script running
Save battery compared with older push
Learn when your device is online, as with classic push
cannot: Send anything before you tap Allow
Run hidden code in the background to do something else
Work in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Samsung Internet
Reach iPhone unless the site is a Home Screen web app
limits.differs: Only Safari on Mac and iPhone supports this format. Other browsers use the classic push format.

story.what_it_is: A push format that shows a notification without running the site's code first.

marketing.name: Declarative Web Push
marketing.pitch: A simpler push format where the browser shows the notice itself, with no background script, for better privacy and battery.

story.for_you: You tap Allow once and notifications show up as usual. Under the hood the browser shows them without waking the site. This saves battery and reduces what the site learns.
story.for_makers: Makers send a ready made message in a set format. It is simpler to build, more reliable and cheaper to run, but gives less control to run code on arrival. It suits news, chat and alerts.

use_cases.example: A news site sends a headline, picture and link in the set format, and Safari shows it with no site code.
A web chat sends a short message notice. Safari shows the sender and text, and the tap opens the thread.
A store sends a shipping update as a ready made notice.
A sports site sends a score alert with a link to the live page.
A browser game sends a turn ready alert without a heavy background script.
A social site sends new follower notices that open the profile on tap.
A bank sends a sign in notice that shows safely with no site script involved.

technical_bounds: Always shows a visible notification (no silent push)
Optional service worker can still adjust the message

history.change: Declarative Web Push ships in iOS and iPadOS 18.4
